subChunks.title: Custom Hooks: Extracting Reusable Logic
subChunks.hookHtml: When the same combination of useState and useEffect appears in three components, it's time to extract a custom hook. Custom hooks let you package stateful logic — fetching, timers, local storage sync, form handling — into a single reusable function. The result: components that are readable, and logic that is testable.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
What is a custom hook?

A custom hook is a JavaScript function whose name starts with use and that calls other hooks. That's the entire definition.

function useWindowWidth() {
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth);

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleResize = () => setWidth(window.innerWidth);
    window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize);
  }, []);

  return width;
}

function ResponsiveLayout() {
  const width = useWindowWidth();
  return <p>{width > 768 ? 'Desktop' : 'Mobile'}</p>;
}

useFetch — the most useful custom hook you'll write

function useFetch(url) {
  const [data, setData] = useState(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    async function load() {
      setLoading(true); setError(null);
      try {
        const res = await fetch(url);
        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
        const json = await res.json();
        if (!cancelled) setData(json);
      } catch (e) {
        if (!cancelled) setError(e.message);
      } finally {
        if (!cancelled) setLoading(false);
      }
    }
    load();
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [url]);

  return { data, loading, error };
}

// Every component that fetches data:
function UserProfile({ userId }) {
  const { data: user, loading, error } = useFetch(`/api/users/${userId}`);
  if (loading) return <p>Loading...</p>;
  if (error)   return <p>Error: {error}</p>;
  return <h2>{user.name}</h2>;
}

useLocalStorage

function useLocalStorage(key, initialValue) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(() => {
    try {
      const stored = localStorage.getItem(key);
      return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : initialValue;
    } catch {
      return initialValue;
    }
  });

  function setStoredValue(newValue) {
    setValue(newValue);
    localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(newValue));
  }

  return [value, setStoredValue];
}

// Drop-in replacement for useState that persists:
const [theme, setTheme] = useLocalStorage('theme', 'light');

When to extract a custom hook

  • The same useState + useEffect combination appears in multiple components
  • A component's logic is complex enough that hook logic dominates readability
  • You want to unit test the logic independently of the UI

Vex: "Custom hooks are the final piece of the Junior bridge. Components describe what to render. Custom hooks contain how to get the data. Keep them separate and both become easier to read, test, and change."

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: When you see the same useState and useEffect combination in three places, that is a custom hook waiting to be written. A custom hook is just a function that starts with 'use' and calls other hooks. Extract it once. Use it everywhere.

storyBeats.speaker: useFetch

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Extract the data-fetching logic into a useFetch(url) custom hook, then use it in a <QuestList> component.

  • useFetch accepts a URL and returns { data, loading, error }
  • It handles loading state, error state, and the race-condition cleanup flag
  • QuestList calls useFetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos?_limit=5') and renders a loading message, error message, or a <ul data-testid="list"> of item titles
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a useLocalStorage(key, initialValue) custom hook from scratch that behaves like useState but persists to localStorage. Then use it in a <ThemeToggle> component that persists 'light' or 'dark' across page refreshes.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain what a custom hook is and why the `use` prefix matters. Walk through how you would extract a repeated fetch pattern into a `useFetch` hook — what does the hook contain, what does it return, and what does the component look like after extraction?

questions.prompt: What are the two requirements for a function to be a React custom hook?
options: Its name must start with `use`, and it must call at least one React hook
It must be defined inside a component and return JSX
It must accept props as its first argument and return state
It must be exported from a separate file
questions.answer: Its name must start with `use`, and it must call at least one React hook
questions.explanation: The `use` prefix lets React's linter and runtime enforce hook rules. Any function starting with `use` that calls useState, useEffect, or other hooks is a valid custom hook.

questions.prompt: Two components call the same custom hook. Do they share state?
options: No — each component gets its own independent state from the hook
Yes — hooks share state between all components that call them
Only if the hook uses useContext internally
Only if both components are rendered by the same parent
questions.answer: No — each component gets its own independent state from the hook
questions.explanation: Custom hooks are not singletons. Each call creates an independent set of state and effects for that specific component instance — same as calling useState directly.

questions.prompt: A component calls `useFetch(url)` with a URL that depends on a prop. What must you ensure?
options: The full URL string must be constructed before passing to useFetch, and the hook's dependency array must include url
Pass the base URL and params separately — useFetch builds the final URL internally
Memoize the URL with useMemo to prevent the effect from re-running
The URL must be a constant — dynamic URLs require a separate useEffect
questions.answer: The full URL string must be constructed before passing to useFetch, and the hook's dependency array must include url
questions.explanation: The component builds the URL: useFetch(`/api/users/${userId}`). The hook's internal effect must have url in its dependency array so it re-fetches when the URL changes.

questions.prompt: When is it NOT appropriate to extract logic into a custom hook?
options: When the logic is used in only one place and is straightforward — the abstraction adds indirection without benefit
When the logic involves more than two useState calls
When the hook would call useEffect
questions.answer: When the logic is used in only one place and is straightforward — the abstraction adds indirection without benefit
questions.explanation: Extract when the pattern repeats or when complexity dominates readability. Don't extract for the sake of cleanliness when there's only one usage — you create a new file, a new abstraction, and no concrete benefit.
